threads.body: as far as I can tell the `getXrayTraceId` method is in `com.amazonaws.services.lambda.runtime.Context` but here the code operates like it was in a subclass. If it really is in `com.amazonaws.services.lambda.runtime.Context` you cold do the method handle lookup only once in a static initializer. Even if the subclass overrides the method calling base class method will end up calling the subclass method, no need to look up the method handle for a subclass.

replies.body: Agreed. I changed this to resolve the method handle once against `com.amazonaws.services.lambda.runtime.Context.class`; invoking that handle on the runtime context will dispatch to the implementation/override when the newer API is present.

threads.body: [General] The linked issue identifies the AWS Lambda 1.4 API as `Context.getTraceHeader()`, but this lookup requests `getXrayTraceId()`. On 1.4 the lookup therefore returns `null`, so the new context value is never added to the carrier; the test’s matching assumption also skips instead of detecting this. Resolve `getTraceHeader` and update the test fixture/assumption to model that API.

replies.body: Fixed in 1215431f9a: the reflective lookup now targets Context.getTraceHeader(), and the latest-deps test fixture/assumption model getTraceHeader() directly. Verified with the focused normal and latest-deps InstrumenterExtractionTest runs.

Did you test this code with an actual lambda? https://github.com/aws/aws-lambda-java-libs does not contain a method named `getTraceHeader` but it contains `getXrayTraceId` Are you sure that the issue isn't just referencing the wrong method name? @wangzlei what is the correct method name?

You are right. I checked aws/aws-lambda-java-libs#563 and the merged change added Context.getXrayTraceId(), not getTraceHeader(); the issue text appears to have the method name wrong. I fixed the PR in 8c19ff1399 to resolve getXrayTraceId() again and updated the latest-deps fixture/assumption to match. The focused normal and latest-deps InstrumenterExtractionTest runs both pass locally.
